questions.question: Which of the following is a common adaptation that helps a prey animal avoid being caught by predators?
options: Having large, sharp claws for hunting
Being nocturnal so they are active in the dark
Having bright, highly visible colors
Emitting loud sounds to signal their location to others

questions.question: Which set of adaptations is most commonly found in predators to help them capture their food?
options: Excellent camouflage and being very slow-moving
Big teeth, good eyesight, and the ability to run fast
The ability to produce edible seeds and store water in stems
Soft bodies, lack of eyes, and feeding on decaying leaves

questions.question: What happens to persistent toxic substances when an organism containing them is eaten by a predator?
options: They are instantly broken down into harmless nutrients.
They are passed up the food chain to the predator.
They are excreted completely without entering the food chain.
They block the transfer of all biomass entirely.

questions.question: Which group of organisms is typically most severely damaged by the bioaccumulation of toxic substances in an ecosystem?
options: Primary producers
Decomposers
Top predators
Microorganisms

questions.question: What components make up an ecosystem?
options: Only the living animals that hunt each other
Only the physical factors like temperature and water
Living organisms interacting and depending on each other, along with their physical environment
Just the plants and the soil they grow in

questions.question: A habitat contains both biotic and abiotic parts. What do these terms mean?
options: Biotic means non-living, and abiotic means living parts
Biotic means living parts, and abiotic means non-living parts
Biotic means large organisms, and abiotic means microscopic organisms
Biotic means predators, and abiotic means prey

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct definition of producers in an ecosystem?
options: Organisms that must hunt other animals to survive
Organisms that can make their own food, such as plants and some microorganisms
Animals that feed only on dead organic matter
Microscopic organisms that only consume other living things

questions.question: How do consumers, such as humans and other animals, obtain their food?
options: By absorbing sunlight directly through their skin
By making their own food from carbon dioxide and water
By eating other organisms because they cannot make their own food
By taking in mineral nutrients directly from the soil

questions.question: In a food chain diagram, what do the arrows pointing from one organism to another represent?
options: The direction of movement of the animals
The transfers of biomass between populations
The evolutionary relationship between the species
The amount of sunlight received by each organism

questions.question: What does a food web diagram represent in an ecosystem?
options: A single, straight-line feeding pathway starting with a predator
The physical migration paths of birds during winter
Several interconnected food chains within a community of organisms
The genetic relationships between different species of plants

questions.question: What occurs during the process of pollination in plants?
options: Seeds are dispersed by wind to new locations
Water is absorbed by the roots and transported to the leaves
Pollen is transferred from the anthers of flowers to the stigma
Fruit is digested by animals to release nutrients

questions.question: Why are pollinators so important for human food security?
options: They directly destroy agricultural pests that eat crops.
They help ensure there is enough food to feed the human population by aiding plant reproduction.
They prevent soil erosion in farming areas.
They purify the water used to irrigate crops.

questions.question: What is meant by the term biodiversity?
options: The total number of individual organisms of a single species in an area
The number of different species that live in a place
The speed at which a population grows in a habitat
The physical size of the largest animals in an ecosystem

questions.question: How can genetic diversity of plants be conserved for the future?
options: By using stronger chemical fertilizers on farms
By removing all predators from natural habitats
Through seed banks and other forms of gene banks
By encouraging the rapid growth of weedy plant species

questions.question: How do certain pesticides help crops grow by targeting other plants?
options: They increase the amount of sunlight the crop receives by making weeds grow taller.
They kill competing plants (weeds) so the crops have less competition to grow.
They convert weeds into high-quality chemical fertilizers.
They attract insect pollinators specifically to the crops.
